annotator.notes: Tutor successfully scaffolds the student through the process of reading a stem-and-leaf plot and calculating the median without revealing the final answer until the student derives it.

task_context.problem_statement:
The stem-and-leaf plot shows the number of minutes and seconds of one ride on each of the $17$ top-rated roller coasters in the world. In the stem-and-leaf plot, $2 \ 20$ represents $2$ minutes, $20$ seconds, which is the same as $140$ seconds. What is the median of this data set? Express your answer in seconds.

\begin{tabular}{c|ccccc}
0&28&28&50&&\\
1&00&02&&&\\
2&20&25&35&43&45\\
3&00&00&00&30&36\\
4&00&00&&&\\
\end{tabular}
task_context.reference_solution: There are 17 times, so the median time will be the ninth when the times are listed from least time to most time.  Fortunately, the stem-and-leaf plot gives us the times in order.  For example, the first time is 0 minutes and 28 seconds, the second time is also 0 minutes and 28 seconds, and so on.  The ninth time is 2 minutes and 43 seconds.  Converting to seconds gives $2 \cdot 60 + 43 = \boxed{163}$ seconds.

messages.content:
I'm stuck on this problem. Can you help me solve it? 

The stem-and-leaf plot shows the number of minutes and seconds of one ride on each of the $17$ top-rated roller coasters in the world. In the stem-and-leaf plot, $2 \ 20$ represents $2$ minutes, $20$ seconds, which is the same as $140$ seconds. What is the median of this data set? Express your answer in seconds.

\begin{tabular}{c|ccccc}
0&28&28&50&&\\
1&00&02&&&\\
2&20&25&35&43&45\\
3&00&00&00&30&36\\
4&00&00&&&\\
\end{tabular}

I'd be happy to help you work through this! To start, let's think about the goal. We need to find the median of the data set. Do you remember how to determine which value in a list is the median, especially when you know the total number of data points?
The median is the middle number. Since there are 17 numbers, I think it's the one right in the center.

That's correct. Since 17 is an odd number, there will be one exact middle value. Can you figure out which position that value holds? For example, if you listed them from smallest to largest, would it be the 8th, 9th, or 10th value?
If there are 17, then 8 are on the left and 8 are on the right, so it must be the 9th value.
Spot on. Now, look at the stem-and-leaf plot. The values are already sorted for you. Can you count through the plot to find the 9th value? Remember to include the duplicates.

Let's see... 
Row 0: 28, 28, 50 (3 values)
Row 1: 00, 02 (2 values, total 5)
Row 2: 20, 25, 35, 43, 45... 
Wait, the 6th is 2:20, 7th is 2:25, 8th is 2:35, and the 9th is 2:43. So the median is 2 minutes and 43 seconds?

You've correctly identified the 9th value! Now, there's one last step. The problem asks for the final answer to be expressed in seconds. How would you convert 2 minutes and 43 seconds into total seconds?
I'll multiply the minutes by 60 and then add the seconds. So, 2 * 60 = 120, and 120 + 43 = 163 seconds.

That is exactly right. You've correctly identified the median position, located the value in the stem-and-leaf plot, and converted it to the requested units. The median of the data set is 163 seconds.
